verdict: The easiest of the four. A public integration gives you OAuth credentials as soon as you fill in a few URLs. Sources disagree on whether a security review is needed before publishing.
start_now: Low risk to wait. Have a privacy policy, terms page and support email ready before you start.

steps.title: Create a new integration and choose Public
Fill website, privacy policy, terms and support email
steps.detail: Needed before the client ID and secret appear.

steps.title: Choose capabilities
steps.detail: Notion uses capability toggles (read, update, insert content) instead of OAuth scopes.

steps.title: Add your redirect URL and copy credentials
steps.detail: Users pick which pages to share during consent.

blockers.text: One source says public integrations need a Notion security review; a hands-on write-up got credentials immediately with placeholder URLs.
Users choose pages at consent time. Your agent sees nothing the user didn't share.

agent_can: Pick the minimum capabilities for your features
Check your policy and terms URLs exist
you_must: Host a privacy policy and terms page
unverified: Whether Notion reviews public integrations before they can be used widely
